title: AP Top 25: LSU rises, Oregon drops and Michigan plummets out of rankings after Week 1
content:
Michigan dropped out of the AP Top 25 college football poll after its controversial, last-second victory against Western Michigan, while No. 8 LSU moved into the top 10 and Oregon slipped four spots to No. 6 on Tuesday.

Ohio State remained a strong No. 1 in the first regular-season poll with 46 first-place votes. With the Ducks falling from No. 2 after a 34-27 home win against Boise State, No. 2 Georgia, No. 3 Notre Dame, No. 4 Texas and No. 5 Indiana all moved up one spot. Miami remained No. 7.

The Buckeyes will face the Longhorns in a top-five matchup Saturday in Austin.

LSU jumped three places from No. 11 after a resounding 51-10 victory against Clemson on Saturday night in the debut of coach Lane Kiffin in Baton Rouge, La.

Ole Miss stayed at No. 9 and Texas A&M rounded out the top 10.

Michigan started the season No. 16, but the Wolverines appeared beaten by heavy underdog Western Michigan on Saturday night in the Big House when a Hail Mary went sailing out of the end zone, seemingly as time expired. A video review put a second back on the clock, and with the extra play Bryce Underwood hit JJ Buchanan with a 47-yard touchdown pass to give Michigan a 13-12 victory. The Mid-American Conference said Tuesday it is appealing the outcome.

Others receiving votes: Boise State 86, Florida 83, Michigan 69, Arizona 33, Memphis 23, South Carolina 19, Western Michigan 12, Pittsburgh 11, Navy 10, UCLA 7, Virginia Tech 6, Illinois 6, James Madison 4, Minnesota 4, Colorado 3, Auburn 2, Arizona State 2, Vanderbilt 2

Overall, there wasn’t much cause for movement in the rankings. The only ranked team that lost was Louisville — and that was to Ole Miss in Week 1’s best game. The Rebels won 41-38 on a last-second field goal. The Cardinals remained No. 24 in this week’s poll.

Michigan was the only team to drop out this week, replaced by Virginia at No. 25.

After one of the chalkiest opening weekends in college football history, with ranked teams going unbeaten against unranked teams, I decided to mostly stand pat. My top 11 from the preseason was unchanged after Week 1, and I made minimal adjustments beyond that.

There were just not enough meaningful games for me to be comfortable rearranging teams.

That meant keeping Oregon at No. 1, which complicated my decision. The Ducks were the one highly ranked team that didn’t waltz to a victory.

Most of the teams at the top barely broke a sweat, playing what amounted to glorified scrimmages. Ranked teams defeated unranked teams by an average of 36 points per game over the long Labor Day weekend.

Notre Dame, LSU and Miami were the weekend’s most impressive teams. Their blowouts at least came against Power 4 competition — though a case could be made that Boise State is better than any of Wisconsin, Clemson and Stanford.

Notre Dame and LSU were the two teams I considered pushing up to No. 1. I had the Irish No. 2 in the preseason and the Tigers No. 8.

But then I thought back to last season and looked at some of my early votes, where making significant moves based on a tiny sample of meaningful games ended up with some regrettable rankings.

I decided to let the season breathe one more week, knowing that Week 2 will produce one significant result that should shake up the top 10: No. 1 Ohio State at No. 4 Texas.

We’ll have to see how the game plays out, but it’s all but certain to impact who’s No. 1 next week.

I did make a couple of changes in the back half of my top 25, most notably: Michigan is out altogether and Boise State is in at No. 20.
